resources.string: Ember Home button
Opens Ember instead of Google TV\'s home screen.

Google TV does not let you choose another Home app. With this on, Ember opens when the TV\'s own home screen comes up: when you press Home, wake the TV or turn it on. In Ember\'s setting \"Catch the Home press\" it also reads the Home key. It reads nothing else, and nothing is stored or sent anywhere. Turn it off here or in Ember\'s Settings > Ember as Home.

Google TV does not let you pick another Home app, so Ember gives you two ways round it, the same ones other launchers use. Method 1 takes a minute on the TV. Method 2 needs a computer or phone once and is the most complete. You can use both.

Method 1: Ember Home button service
No computer needed. Support depends on the TV firmware.
1. Press Open Accessibility settings below.
2. Find Ember Home button (on some TVs under Downloaded services or Services) and switch it on. Accept the warning: Android shows it for every accessibility service.
3. Press Back to return here. \"Right now\" above should say the service is on.
4. Press Home on the remote to try it.
Open Accessibility settings
This TV has no Accessibility settings screen Ember can open. Look in Settings > System > Accessibility.
Open Ember instead of Google TV\'s home
Uses the service above. Switch off to keep the service but leave Home alone.
How
When Google TV\'s home appears
Catch the Home press
Google TV\'s home may show for a moment first. Long-press Home still opens the TV\'s quick panel.
Ember opens straight away. Google TV\'s home is still caught when the TV wakes or starts. Long-press Home also opens Ember.
Open Ember when the TV starts
The TV starts the service when it powers on; Ember opens then.
Open Google TV home once
Left alone for one minute, e.g. to change Google TV\'s own settings.
The TV\'s own home screen is turned off or missing.
If it stops working after a Google TV update: switch Ember Home button off in Accessibility, wait a few seconds and switch it on again. Some updates also switch accessibility services off.
Method 2: turn off Google TV\'s home (ADB)
Once done, the TV has no other Home app, so Home, waking and start-up all open Ember with nothing in between. Needs a computer with ADB (Android platform tools) or an ADB app on your phone, once.
1. Turn on Developer options: Settings > System > About, select Android TV OS build seven times.
2. In Settings > System > Developer options, switch on USB debugging (or Wireless debugging on Android 11 and later, then Pair device with pairing code).
3. On the computer or phone, on the same network, run:
4. Allow the connection on the TV when it asks. After the restart, Home opens Ember.
Wireless debugging: first run \"adb pair\" with the address and code shown on the TV, then \"adb connect\" with the address shown there.

Connect the TV to your network to see its address.
To undo

With Google TV\'s home off you lose what only it does: the Google TV profile picker, For you and Apps only mode. Voice search on the remote, the TV\'s settings, casting and every app still work. A big Google TV update can switch it back on; run the commands again, and keep Method 1 on as a backup.
Method 3: choose the Home app
Android TV and some TVs let you pick the Home app in their settings. On Google TV the screen is missing or greyed out, which is why Methods 1 and 2 exist.
